title: Father, into Thy Hands Alone
description: Father, into Thy Hands Alone in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 432. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, in-to thy hands a-lone I have my all re-stored; My all thy prop-er-ty I own, The stew-ard of the Lord.

lines: My all thy property I own,
My life, or goods, or fame;
Ready at thy demand to lay
I wait thy faithfulness to prove,
And give back all to thee.
Take when thou wilt into thy hands,
Determined all thy will to obey,
Give, Lord, or take thy gifts away,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
